topStories.headline: Alice Griffith Tenants Describe Rat Infestation, Debt Notices as Pelosi Calls Conditions 'Deeply Concerning'
topStories.dek: Residents of the Bayview–Hunters Point affordable housing complex say conditions have worsened despite months of public hearings and promises of remediation.
topStories.body:
Tenants at Alice Griffith Apartments in Bayview–Hunters Point say a severe rodent infestation persists even after the property's owner declared the problem exterminated. According to Mission Local reporting published July 23, 2026, one resident said she was startled by a rat "the size of a cat" only days after management said the rodents were gone, and another reported seeing a rodent as recently as July 20. When Mission Local reporters visited the 2500 building on July 21, an intense smell emanated from the first floor, debris lay piled in the trash room, and the building's garage remained stuck ajar.

The crisis at Alice Griffith — a federally subsidized, LEED-certified complex built as a flagship of the Candlestick Point/Hunters Point Shipyard redevelopment — has drawn widening political attention. On July 14, 2026, tenants received debt-due notices taped to their apartment doors, a development that advocacy journalists and tenant organizers have called retaliatory. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, who once heralded the construction of Alice Griffith, issued a statement calling tenants' allegations "deeply concerning," according to Mission Local.

The San Francisco Housing Authority has documented more than 129 deficiencies at the property in a single year, including broken elevators, electrical hazards, pest infestations, and plumbing failures, according to reporting by the Davis Vanguard. A disabled resident described being trapped in his apartment for nine days when elevators stopped functioning. Advocacy journalists have called for an independent audit of the property's management records and a moratorium on eviction filings arising from the July 14 balance-due notices until habitability obligations are confirmed as being met.

Tenant advocates and Open Door Legal, which maintains an office on Third Street in Bayview, have pledged to support residents through legal channels. The ongoing crisis has become one of the most closely watched affordable-housing accountability stories in San Francisco, with multiple city agencies, building managers, and elected officials named in public scrutiny of the situation.

topStories.headline: Excelsior's Mission Street and Geneva Avenue Get a Safety Makeover After Nearly Four Years of Construction
topStories.dek: A $31 million multi-agency infrastructure project has wrapped up, delivering 87 new curb ramps, 70 new traffic signals, and fresh pavement to two of the neighborhood's most dangerous corridors.
topStories.body:
San Francisco officials gathered at Mission and Norton streets on July 11, 2026 to celebrate the completion of the Mission Street and Geneva Avenue Infrastructure Improvement Project, a nearly four-year effort to overhaul two of the Excelsior's most dangerous and heavily traveled corridors. The project was a collaboration among the San Francisco Department of Public Works, the SFMTA, and the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission.

Public Works Director Carla Short said the project delivered 87 new curb ramps, 70 new traffic signals, 34 bulb-outs, 22 streetlight replacements, 17 concrete bus pads, three bus bulbs, and two raised crosswalks, along with tens of thousands of square feet of new concrete and thousands of tons of fresh asphalt, according to a statement reported by KTVU. The project area covered Mission Street from Geneva Avenue to the Interstate 280 overpass and Geneva Avenue from Prague Street to Mission Street.

Both streets are part of San Francisco's Vision Zero High Injury Network — the 13 percent of city streets where 75 percent of all severe and fatal collisions occur. In the seven years prior to construction, five people were killed and at least 323 were injured in the project area, according to KTVU. The eight Muni lines serving the neighborhood have average speeds below five miles per hour, and the new bus bulbs and transit infrastructure are intended to improve reliability.

District 11 Supervisor Chayanne Chen said the project will help improve the lives of those who live in and visit the area. Mayor Daniel Lurie called the Excelsior "one of the most tight-knit neighborhoods in the city" and said improvements like these give residents confidence to move through their community on foot, by bike, on Muni, or in a car, according to a press release cited by KTVU.

topStories.headline: Black-Owned Bookstore and Café 'Chapter 3' Coming to Bayview's Third Street
topStories.dek: Vanessa Lee, owner of Smoke Soul Kitchen, has filed a permit application to open the neighborhood's first general-interest bookstore since Marcus Books left the area.
topStories.body:
Bayview–Hunters Point is set to get its first general-interest bookstore in years. Vanessa Lee, the owner of Smoke Soul Kitchen on Third Street, has filed a permit application to open Chapter 3 — a Black-owned bookstore and café — at 4512 3rd Street, between La Salle Avenue and Third Street, according to Mission Local reporting from July 2026.

Lee told Mission Local she was inspired by Marcus Books, a Black-owned bookstore that once operated in the Fillmore before relocating to Oakland. "I saw how it brought the community together," Lee said. She added that she wanted to create "a place that people will really like and that we deserve." The last bookstore in Bayview–Hunters Point, Just A Touch Christian Bookstore, closed more than two years ago after struggling to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic.

The hybrid café and bookstore will occupy a former MetroPCS storefront. Lee plans to serve food at the café, including weekend brunch, and to operate a wine bar in the evenings. She also intends to host author readings and live performances, according to Shelf Awareness. Chapter 3 is one of nine Bayview businesses to receive a Storefront Opportunity Grant from the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development this year.

Lee plans to open Chapter 3 by the end of 2026, which would make it the sole bookstore serving Bayview–Hunters Point's roughly 35,000 residents. The announcement comes as Third Street continues a commercial revival that has added more than 25 new businesses and nonprofits since 2021, according to 7x7.

events.title: 24th Annual Jerry Day Free Music Festival

events.description: The 24th annual Jerry Day returns to the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater in McLaren Park with a free all-day celebration of Excelsior native Jerry Garcia. This year's lineup features Melvin Seals & JGB with Jazz Mafia, Stu Allen & Mars Hotel, and Spencer Krenz & Friends, with an all-ages Sunset Mercantile fun zone on-site; Excelsior neighborhood after-parties run from 5–10 PM.

events.title: Sunday Streets Bayview — Free Car-Free Block Party

moreNews.headline: Crocker Amazon Ballfields May Be Renamed Willie Mays Fields of Champions in $50M Giants-Backed Overhaul
moreNews.body: The San Francisco Recreation and Park Commission has unanimously recommended that the Board of Supervisors accept a $28 million grant from the San Francisco Giants to fund a $50 million renovation of Crocker Amazon Park's baseball and softball complex. If the board approves the deal, the fields would be renamed the Willie Mays Fields of Champions, with a $5 million lead gift from Mays' Say Hey Foundation. The project would add batting cages, new lighting, and additional fields, expanding access to play by up to 10,000 hours per year, according to SF Rec and Park. The proposal remains contested: the community group Keep Crocker Real has gathered hundreds of signatures opposing the plan's reliance on artificial turf and tree removal, while District 11 Supervisor Chayanne Chen has called for more community input before final approval. Construction could begin as early as 2027 if environmental review and Board of Supervisors approval proceed.

moreNews.headline: Bayview Residents Still Without a Local Pharmacy More Than a Year After Walgreens Closure
moreNews.body: Bayview–Hunters Point residents continue to travel outside their neighborhood for prescription medications and pharmacy services, more than one year after the area's last Walgreens closed, according to Mission Local. The pharmacy desert adds to longstanding concerns about health-service access in a neighborhood that already faces environmental health burdens and a high concentration of residents with chronic conditions. Community advocates have repeatedly called on the city and private pharmacy chains to fill the gap, so far without a public commitment from any provider.

moreNews.headline: Win Long Hardware on Ocean Avenue Earns San Francisco Legacy Business Status
moreNews.body: Win Long Hardware, a community fixture on Ingleside's Ocean Avenue since 2014, has been added to San Francisco's Legacy Business Registry, the Ingleside Light reported. Owner Julie Chin's store — which carries tools, paint supplies, locks, and household goods — was nominated through its sister store on Irving Street, which qualified the Ocean Avenue location after decades in the family business. The store was the first hardware shop to return to the Ocean View–Merced Heights–Ingleside area after a 25-year gap, and was also the first in the neighborhood to serve the growing Asian community with Chinese-speaking employees.

restaurants.name: El Farolito

restaurants.name: Taqueria Guadalajara
restaurants.description: Excelsior neighborhood taqueria known for customizable carnitas burritos, tacos, and fresh salsas at fair prices.

restaurants.name: Pupusería Metapán

restaurants.name: Ocean Subs
restaurants.description: Excelsior sub shop with a devoted local following for its perfectly calibrated Dutch-crunch sandwiches stacked with Italian meats, vegetables, and tangy herb vinaigrette.

restaurants.name: Calabria Brothers
restaurants.description: Excelsior institution serving enormous Italian deli sandwiches from a classic counter in the heart of the neighborhood.

restaurants.name: Tala Natural Wine Bar
restaurants.description: Small Excelsior natural wine bar with a long list of imported and domestic wines, a communal neighborhood vibe, and rotating small-plate accompaniments.

restaurants.name: Pho Golden
restaurants.description: Casual Excelsior Vietnamese spot especially praised for dishes featuring grilled pork and house-made broths.

restaurants.name: Beep's Burgers
restaurants.description: Ingleside drive-in institution open since 1962, beloved for juicy burgers, curly fries, and creamy milkshakes served through a walk-up window.

restaurants.name: Ocean Ale House
restaurants.description: Welcoming all-ages brewery and bar on Ocean Avenue with live music, rotating craft taps, and a menu of bar food that draws a convivial local crowd.

restaurants.name: Pakwan

restaurants.name: Java On Ocean

restaurants.description: Solid, cash-only Thai spot in the Excelsior serving authentic curries, noodle dishes, and stir-fries in a no-frills setting.

shops.name: Win Long Hardware

shops.name: Ocean Cyclery
shops.description: Family-owned Legacy bike shop in the Ingleside area carrying road, mountain, electric, and cargo bikes, plus full repair and custom build services.

shops.name: Chapter 3 Bookstore & Café
shops.description: Forthcoming Black-owned bookstore, café, and wine bar from Smoke Soul Kitchen owner Vanessa Lee — the first general-interest bookstore in Bayview–Hunters Point in years, slated to open in late 2026.

shops.description: Neighborhood specialty grocery on Ocean Avenue bringing unique Mexican and Latin American pantry items, fresh produce, and imported goods to Ingleside.

shops.name: Serge a Lot

shops.name: The Plant Lady SF

artEntertainment.name: Ruth Williams Bayview Opera House
artEntertainment.type: Historic community theater and cultural center
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest surviving theater (est. 1888), a National Register landmark and City Designated Landmark No. 8, serving as the performing arts and cultural hub of Bayview–Hunters Point with concerts, art exhibits, youth programs, and community events.

artEntertainment.name: Jerry Garcia Amphitheater

artEntertainment.description: Newly opened 2.5-acre waterfront park at 900 Innes Avenue giving Bayview–Hunters Point residents public access to the bay for the first time in generations, with an Artist-in-Residence program run in partnership with the San Francisco Arts Commission.

artEntertainment.name: The Church of Clown
artEntertainment.description: Bayview-area alternative performance venue hosting live music, theater, and avant-garde events along Bayshore Boulevard.

artEntertainment.name: All Good Pizza
artEntertainment.type: Pizza venue and community event space

gymsRecreation.description: Full-service YMCA offering fitness facilities, indoor and outdoor pools, a gymnasium, youth and senior programs, aquatics, and arts and humanities classes serving the Bayview–Hunters Point community.

gymsRecreation.name: Crocker Amazon Playground and Recreation Center

gymsRecreation.name: Coffman Pool (McLaren Park)
gymsRecreation.description: SF Recreation and Parks public pool at the southeastern entrance of McLaren Park, offering recreational swim, learn-to-swim classes, water aerobics, and underwater hockey.

gymsRecreation.name: Herz Recreation Center
gymsRecreation.description: Newly opened 11,500-square-foot community gymnasium in McLaren Park featuring a full-size basketball court with bleacher seating for 200, a multipurpose room for wellness classes and rentals, and childcare facilities serving Sunnydale and Visitacion Valley.

gymsRecreation.name: McLaren Park Tennis Complex
gymsRecreation.description: Six outdoor public tennis courts situated on the upper portion of McLaren Park at Mansell and Visitacion Streets, free to the public and open daily.

gymsRecreation.name: Yoga Flow SF — Ocean Avenue
gymsRecreation.description: Hot yoga studio occupying a former Masonic temple on Ocean Avenue in Ingleside, offering a full schedule of heated vinyasa and power yoga classes.

gymsRecreation.name: McLaren Park Mountain Bike Park
gymsRecreation.description: Half-acre mountain bike park on the south end of Sunnydale Avenue completed in 2017, with trails and features serving riders from Excelsior, Crocker Amazon, Visitacion Valley, and beyond.
gymsRecreation.address: Sunnydale Ave, McLaren Park, San Francisco, CA 94134
